lab_table.hypothesis: Source-size-matching hypothesis: missed inclusions are small (median 33.8px) while train sources average 90.5px; weighting smaller inclusion sources (prefer_small) at default scale should shift the paste size distribution toward the missed range without the downscaling artifacts that may have hurt the round-1 small-scale combo. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 > 0.335 and mAP50 > 0.5746 with scratches holding >= 0.59.

Scratches background-diversity hypothesis: the inclusion-heavy allocation cost scratches ~0.04 AP50 (0.643 balanced vs 0.602 heavy); pasting scratches onto any_class backgrounds (cleaner/more varied contexts) should recover part of that loss without giving up inclusion allocation. Confirmed if scratches AP50 >= 0.62 with inclusion AP50 unchanged (~0.33) and mAP50 > 0.5746.

Inclusion small-scale isolation (uncertain alternative): round 1 showed small scale helped inclusion in the balanced setting but the all-small heavy-allocation combo was worse; this tests small scale for inclusion ONLY (0.3-0.7, same as round 1) with patches/scratches at default. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 > 0.335 and low-tertile recall rises; if it ties/loses to control, smallness is ruled out for inclusion under heavy allocation and round 3 should focus on allocation/backgrounds.
CONTROL (added by the lab): repeat your last kept plan (allocation projected onto this round's constraints).

lesson: Cumulative default inclusion-heavy synthetic compounds strongly (control +0.059 just from adding more). Small-scale inclusion (0.3-0.7x downscaling of large sources) is the real lever: best inclusion/worst-class AP50 (0.493) at ~no mAP50 cost — KEEP it; but prefer_small inclusion SOURCES and any_class scratch backgrounds are both big net losses (mAP50 -0.05/-0.06 vs control), so avoid them. Round 3: build on small-scale inclusion and try to recover the patches dip (-0.085 vs control) via a bit more patches allocation or default-scale patches, while confirming small-scale inclusion holds.
